You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Optical Communication Names Including Lumentum and Corning Advance; Nvidia Beats Estimates, Rises Over 4% After Hours; Marvell Reports After the Close (August 27, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
July PCE Runs Hot; Walsh’s Jackson Hole Speech Arrives Tonight
U.S. July PCE rose 3.7% year-over-year and 0.2% month-over-month, both above expectations, reconfirming inflation stickiness.
The Jackson Hole global central-bank symposium opens Thursday ET; Fed Chair Kevin Walsh delivers the keynote on Friday.
CME data still show holding rates unchanged in September as the baseline scenario, but the hot inflation print makes hike pricing difficult to fully fade.
Market Impact : Hotter PCE weighed on near-term risk appetite. Walsh’s speech is the week’s most important policy-communication window and will directly affect term premiums and growth-stock pricing.
International Commodities
Trump Says No Timetable for Iran Talks; Diplomacy and Pressure Run in Parallel
In an interview, President Trump said he has “no timetable and is in no hurry” for Iran to return to the negotiating table, while arguing Iran faces severe inflation and a collapsing economy.
Energy Secretary Wright said Washington prefers a diplomatic solution but would destroy Iran’s nuclear facilities if necessary.
Iranian President Pezeshkian responded that current U.S. economic pressure will not succeed.
Market Impact : Expectations of a rapid geopolitical thaw have cooled, giving oil some support. Reassessment risk around the inflation path has risen, increasing near-term commodity volatility.
Macroeconomic Policy
Data-Center Delay Risk Rises; White House Advances Drug-Pricing Deals
Kimmeridge co-founder Ben Dell estimates that as many as half of planned U.S. data centers could be delayed or canceled because of political opposition, litigation and physical-infrastructure constraints.
The White House plans a new round of “most-favored-nation” drug-pricing agreements with several mid-sized biotech firms, covering Medicaid discounts.
President Trump signed an executive order restricting certain foreign-made large power-system equipment from entering the U.S. grid.
Market Impact : The pace of AI infrastructure deployment faces real-world constraints, drawing attention to power and domestic-equipment themes. Drug-pricing agreements create a policy variable for related pharmaceutical names.
II. Market Review
Commodities Forex Performance
Spot Gold : Approx. $4,605/oz, +0.23%
Spot Silver : Approx. $68.7/oz, +0.28%
WTI Crude : Approx. $81.9/bbl, -0.4%
Brent Crude : Approx. $84.68/bbl, -0.48%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approx. 99.11, -0.03%
Driver Analysis : The hotter July PCE print reinforced the sticky-inflation narrative and provided some support for precious metals. Trump’s comment that there is no timetable for Iran talks prevented geopolitical premiums from fading further, helping oil stabilize. Institutional views hold that near-term commodities are jointly driven by “hot inflation + geopolitical uncertainty,” with the linkage running from a hotter PCE → repricing of real rates and the policy path → gold attracting haven and store-of-value demand, while oil is underpinned by geopolitics.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. $78,785, +0.15%
ETH : Approx. $2,494, +1.8%
Crypto Total Market Cap : $2.74 trillion, +0.5%
Market Liquidations : 24-hour liquidations $285 million, of which short liquidations $136 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : BTC currently around $78,700. Significant short-liquidation pressure is clustered in the $79,500–$80,000 zone above; a break of $80,000 could trigger a sizable short squeeze. Long-liquidation levels are relatively dense in the $76,500–$78,000 zone below; a break of $78,000 could accelerate leveraged-long liquidations. Short-term volatility remains elevated.
Spot ETF Net Flows : Yesterday’s net inflow $314 million; current 24-hour dynamic net inflow $31.4 million.
Driver Analysis : Hotter PCE and cautious risk-asset sentiment exerted some near-term pressure on crypto, but the “currency debasement trade” narrative remains intact. Bernstein positions Bitcoin as a core hard-asset beneficiary and maintains a $300,000 year-end 2029 target. Institutional consensus points to high-level consolidation; attention remains on liquidity and risk-appetite shifts after Walsh’s speech.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 53,463.88, -0.21%
SP 500 : Closed at 7,675.70, -0.02%
Nasdaq : Closed at 26,130.20, -0.08%, awaiting digestion of Nvidia’s guidance
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $210.00, -1.43% (after-hours approx. $218.50, up more than 4%)
AAPL : $315.20, +1.71%
MSFT : $496.50, +0.97%
GOOGL : $342.03, -1.42%
AMZN : $260.31, -0.29%
META : $576.37, +1.11%
TSLA : $345.65, -1.31%
[...]
Performance Summary Driver Analysis : Hotter PCE left the three major indexes slightly lower as capital stayed cautious ahead of Nvidia’s report. Storage and optical-communication sectors continued to strengthen, and cybersecurity stocks advanced broadly. Nvidia’s after-hours beat and FY2028 growth guidance of about 70% significantly lifted sentiment, pushing tech futures higher. Individual-stock divergence shifted from “macro caution” toward “company-level fundamental validation.”
[...]
1. Nvidia (NVDA) – Large Q2 Beat and Rare Long-Dated Guidance
[...]
Event Overview : Nvidia reported FY2027 Q2 revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year-over-year, and adjusted EPS of $2.22, up 120%. Data-center revenue reached $89.0 billion, up 117% and above estimates. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75.0%. CFO Colette Kress unusually guided FY2028 revenue growth of about 70% versus prior analyst expectations of roughly 44%, adding that the outlook would be “much higher” without supply constraints. CEO Jensen Huang said demand growth is approaching 100% and that the 70% figure is a conservative estimate based on current supply capacity. Shares rose more than 4% after hours.
[...]
2. Apple (AAPL) – Foldable Launch Set for September 10
[...]
Event Overview : Apple confirmed its autumn launch event for 1:00 a.m. Beijing time on September 10, under the slogan “Surprise and Shine.” Markets expect the first foldable iPhone as well as iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with faster chips and longer battery life. The event will be new CEO John Ternus’s first major product showcase.
[...]
3. Meta (META) – Settlement of Up to About $18 Billion With Multiple States
[...]
Event Overview : Meta agreed to pay up to about $18 billion to settle landmark litigation with multiple U.S. states over social media’s impact on minors.
[...]
Apple confirmed its September 10 autumn event, with markets focused on the first foldable iPhone.
[...]
Meta reached a settlement of up to about $18 billion with multiple U.S. states over social-media litigation.
[...]
Investment-bank analysts argue that hotter July PCE keeps markets alert to inflation stickiness, but Nvidia’s large beat and unusually long-dated growth guidance have materially repaired the AI-demand narrative. Trump’s comment that there is no timetable for Iran talks makes it harder for geopolitical premiums to fade further. Storage and optical communication continue to display relative strength as bottleneck segments. Crypto is consolidating at elevated levels within a “debasement trade” framework. Overall strategy recommendation: treat Walsh’s speech and the delivery of Nvidia’s guidance as the near-term core variables; stay flexible on high-valuation growth stocks while watching power equipment, storage and optical communication—segments with genuine supply constraints.
